title: Conference abstract scraper
description: Produce clean, structured, searchable JSON for a conference's accepted posters/abstracts by combining CrossRef (canonical metadata: DOI, authors, publication date, issue ordering) with the conference's own Confex meeting program (full abstract text) — deliberately bypassing publisher sites that are frequently WAF/Cloudflare-blocked. Includes a completeness check that guarantees no entry is skipped, merged, or duplicated.

cta.label: Fork and run
cta.note: Runs on Jetty's managed sandbox. No setup. Free for your first 10 runs.

example_outputs.title: JSCAI 2026 issue, top 20 abstracts
example_outputs.summary: 20 cardiovascular-intervention conference abstracts sourced from CrossRef (metadata/ordering) + the SCAI Confex program (full text) directly, 19 PASS / 1 PARTIAL, 0 duplicates.

outputs.description: 20 structured abstract records with metadata and full text.
Stage results, completeness check, and overall_passed.

inputs.label: CrossRef ISSN
inputs.description: The journal's ISSN, used to query CrossRef for the target issue's DOIs, titles, authors, and publication dates.

inputs.label: CrossRef volume/issue
inputs.description: The specific volume/issue to pull from CrossRef.

inputs.label: Confex program URL
inputs.description: The conference's own Confex meeting program — the primary full-text source.

inputs.label: Max abstracts
inputs.description: Number of abstracts to process, in CrossRef page-number order.

metrics._note: Live counters — supplied by the Jetty backend at render time, not authored here.

caveats: Full text is sourced from the conference's own Confex program, which is normally a pre-publication version — it may differ slightly from the eventual published version in wording or completeness.
One entry in this example (1/20) had only a short excerpt available in the Confex program and is marked PARTIAL rather than PASS.

The Confex program URL and session names (e.g. 'Coronary', 'Oral Abstracts') are conference- and year-specific — check the conference's public program page for the current URL if targeting a different year or event.
